items.desc: DM me the word 'PLATES’ on my IG and I’ll send you my training on how to eat more to lose fat after 35. If you’re a high-performing woman who’s doing everything right and your body still isn’t reacting like it used to, the plate is the first place to look. Why each pick lands where it does: Carbs: Rice on its own digests fast and leaves you hungry again. Oats and potatoes keep your blood sugar steady, so you’re not digging through the pantry at 3pm. Fats: Trail mix is mostly candy and dried fruit, and it disappears fast while you answer emails. Almonds come with fiber and protein. Salmon adds protein and omega-3 fats that keep you full for hours. Drinks: A restaurant margarita can run 300 to 500 calories with a sugar crash on top. Dry white wine and a vodka soda with lime sit around 100 to 120 with no sugar. Alcohol still pauses fat burning, so pick your drink on purpose. Olive oil: A shot on an empty stomach is 120 calories of fat with nothing to keep you full. A tablespoon on your veggies, or a few sprays from a mister, gets you the benefit without the guessing. Lunch: The plain desk salad is usually behind the 9pm pantry raid. Add protein and a real carb and the afternoon changes. Nothing here asks you to eat less. The effortless foods fill you up and steady your blood sugar, which lets you eat more while your metabolism rebuilds. DM me the word "PLATES” on my IG and I’ll send it over. Stick to the plan and embrace that uncomfortable feeling. It will suck, but you will be ok. It’ll all be worth it in the end.

A year ago, I weighed 72 kg. Today, I’m around 55 kg. In total, I’ve lost about 44 lbs (20 kg) since having my second baby. And the most interesting part? I finally started seeing results when I stopped trying to do EVERYTHING at once. I used to work out a lot, eat healthy, and still struggle with my weight. These 5 changes are what actually transformed my body: 1. I FOCUSED ON REAL STRENGTH TRAINING. 3 workouts a week, the same core exercises, and I progressively increased the weights instead of constantly adding more exercises. Squats, Romanian deadlifts, hip thrusts, and step-ups. MUSCLE is what changed my body shape, not sweating more. 2. I STOPPED RELYING ONLY ON “CLEAN EATING” AND STARTED PAYING ATTENTION TO CALORIES AND MACROS. Just because you’re eating healthy foods doesn’t mean you’re in a calorie deficit. Once I started paying attention to how much I was eating, including protein, fats, and carbs, I could finally understand where those extra calories were coming from. 3. I PUT PROTEIN FIRST AT EVERY MEAL. My goal is 120–150g of protein a day! In practice, that means eggs, fish, meat, chicken, and seafood. I always prioritize getting enough protein before adding everything else to my plate. It keeps me full longer and helps me maintain the muscle I’ve worked so hard to build. I LOVE protein, so eating this way is perfect for ME! 4. I ATE IN A SMALL CALORIE DEFICIT AND STOPPED STARTING OVER EVERY MONDAY. Around 300–400 calories below maintenance. A small deficit is something you can actually stick to long-term. That’s what finally helped me stop constantly struggling with my weight. One meal that doesn’t fit your usual routine is NOT a reason to start all over again. 5. I WALKED EVERY SINGLE DAY. 10,000 steps. Over a week, walking adds up to a significant amount of extra movement and calorie expenditure. And for me, it doesn’t leave me starving the way intense cardio sessions sometimes did. WHAT I DIDN’T DO: I didn’t train 6 days a week or force myself to do endless cardio. I chose simple, real food, strength training, and daily movement. I also weighed myself regularly, measured my waist, and tracked changes in my body. The scale can stay the same for weeks while your waist gets smaller and your clothes start fitting completely differently. And I did all of this at 37. Today, I still follow these same 5 principles. 💛 Follow @nataly_run for more and SAVE this post! #weightlossjourneys #fatloss #weightlossafter40 #strengthtraining #highprotein
